cls: Recombinant type I interferon (interferon alfa-2a); immunomodulator / antiviral / antineoplastic
pharm: Highly purified recombinant interferon alfa-2a (a ~19 kDa, 165-amino-acid protein produced in E. coli) that binds type I interferon receptors to trigger antiproliferative, antiviral, and immunomodulatory intracellular signaling, used parenterally (subcutaneous, with IM historically for Kaposi sarcoma) in million international units (MIU).
quick: Indication-specific in MIU SC: hairy cell leukemia 3 MIU daily x16-24wk then 3 MIU 3x/wk; hepatitis C 3 MIU 3x/wk; CML 9 MIU daily
Category C; abortifacient in primates; use only if benefit justifies risk; effective contraception required
Excretion in milk unknown; decide to discontinue nursing or drug
Use with caution if CrCl <50 mL/min; severe renal toxicity (sometimes needing dialysis) reported
Contraindicated in hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh B/C) and autoimmune hepatitis
Avoid; adds hepatotoxic and CNS-depressant burden in patients with liver disease
CBC, LFTs, TSH/thyroid, neuropsychiatric status, eye exam, triglycerides, cardiac
summary: Interferon alfa-2a (Roferon-A) is a recombinant type I interferon given subcutaneously (historically intramuscularly for Kaposi sarcoma) in million international units. FDA-approved indications include hairy cell leukemia, chronic phase Philadelphia-chromosome-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), and chronic hepatitis C in adults with compensated liver disease; older labeling also included AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma. It carries a BOXED WARNING that alpha-interferons cause or aggravate fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders; patients must be monitored closely and withdrawn if signs persist or worsen. A flu-like syndrome (fever, fatigue, myalgia, headache, chills) is the most common toxicity. It is contraindicated in hepatic decompensation, autoimmune hepatitis, and in neonates/infants (benzyl alcohol). Dosing is indication-specific and modified (typically 50% reduction or interruption) for toxicity, with close hematologic, hepatic, thyroid, neuropsychiatric, ophthalmologic, and cardiac monitoring.
indications: Hairy cell leukemia in patients 18 years of age or older
Chronic phase, Philadelphia chromosome (Ph)-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in adults who are minimally pretreated (within 1 year of diagnosis)
Chronic hepatitis C in patients 18 years of age or older with compensated liver disease, after excluding other causes (e.g., hepatitis B)
AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma in select patients (older labeling); not for visceral AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma

dosage.n: Discontinue if no response within 6 months; doses higher than 3 MIU are not recommended
May continue up to 24 consecutive months

dosage.d: 3 MIU three times a week for 12 months; alternative 6 MIU 3x/wk x3 months then 3 MIU 3x/wk x9 months
dosage.n: Consider stopping if no response by 3 months; relapse retreatment 3-6 MIU 3x/wk for 6-12 months

dosage.d: 9 MIU daily; escalate over first week (3 MIU/day x3d, then 6 MIU/day x3d, then 9 MIU/day) to improve tolerance
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression; median time to hematologic response ~5 months

dosage.d: 36 MIU daily for 10 to 12 weeks (SC preferred if platelets <50,000 or bleeding risk)
dosage.n: Doses above 36 MIU/day caused unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: Reduce dose by 50% or interrupt until adverse events resolve, then re-escalate; discontinue if reduced dose not tolerated
dosage.n: Discontinue if neutrophils <0.5 x10^9/L or platelets <25 x10^9/L

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection (intramuscular only for the historical Kaposi sarcoma regimen)
Rotate subcutaneous injection sites; teach proper self-injection technique and safe sharps disposal
Do not switch between different brands of interferon within a single treatment course without medical consultation - dosage and adverse reactions differ
Keep patients well hydrated, especially during the early phase of therapy
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; protect from light
Do not use formulations containing benzyl alcohol in neonates or infants
moa: Interferon alfa-2a is a recombinant single-species type I interferon that binds to the type I (alpha/beta) interferon cell-surface receptor, activating JAK-STAT signaling and inducing interferon-stimulated genes. The exact antitumor and antiviral mechanism is not fully understood but is believed to involve a direct antiproliferative effect on tumor cells, inhibition of viral replication in infected cells, and modulation of the host immune response (enhanced macrophage phagocytosis, augmented NK-cell and lymphocyte cytotoxicity). Its biologic activities are species-restricted. These same immunostimulatory and inflammatory actions underlie the flu-like syndrome and the neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious toxicities highlighted in the boxed warning.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to interferon alfa-2a or any component of the product
Hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh class B and C) before or during treatment
Neonates and infants (formulations containing benzyl alcohol - risk of fatal neurologic complications)
relative: History of depression, psychiatric illness, or suicidal ideation/behavior
Pre-existing cardiac disease (arrhythmia, ischemia, heart failure)
Pre-existing ophthalmologic disorders such as diabetic or hypertensive retinopathy
monitor: Neuropsychiatric status, especially depression and suicidality
Eye examination at baseline and for new ocular symptoms
Cardiac function (ECG) in those with cardiac disease or advanced cancer

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Interferon alfa-2a produced a statistically significant, dose-related increase in abortions in pregnant rhesus monkeys (no teratogenic effects observed). There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Women of childbearing potential and men should use effective contraception during therapy. Benzyl alcohol in some formulations crosses the placenta - use caution near delivery.
lact: It is not known whether interferon alfa-2a is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a nursing infant, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Dose-limiting renal toxicity is unusual, but severe renal toxicities (sometimes requiring dialysis) have been reported, alone or in combination with interleukin-2. Use with caution in patients with creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min and monitor closely for interferon toxicity. Alfa interferons are filtered through the glomeruli and undergo proteolytic degradation during tubular reabsorption, with negligible systemic reappearance.
hepatic: Contraindicated in patients with hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh class B and C) and in autoimmune hepatitis. In chronic hepatitis C, initiation can cause transient liver function abnormalities; in patients with poorly compensated disease this may precipitate increased ascites, hepatic failure, or death. Rarely associated with severe hepatic dysfunction and liver failure; discontinue if hepatic function deteriorates.

major: Zidovudine (AZT) and other myelosuppressive agents - synergistic myelosuppression; use combination with caution
Interleukin-2 - concurrent use may potentiate the risk of renal failure
moderate: Theophylline - interferon reduces theophylline clearance; monitor levels
CNS-active / centrally acting drugs - potential additive neurotoxicity
CYP450 substrates - interferon may reduce hepatic microsomal cytochrome P450 activity, altering metabolism of concomitant drugs
minor: Immunosuppressants in transplant patients - interferon's immunostimulatory effect may weaken therapeutic immunosuppression
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction (parenteral drug); maintain good hydration.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - it adds hepatotoxic burden in patients with liver disease and may compound CNS depression and depression risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May induce or worsen thyroid dysfunction altering thyroid function tests; can cause development of autoantibodies (e.g., antinuclear, antithyroid).

serious: Severe depression and suicidal ideation or attempts
emergency: Suicidal ideation or attempt / acute psychosis
Acute colitis (abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, fever)

monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets - baseline and routinely (very careful during first 1-3 months); discontinue if neutrophils <0.5 x10^9/L or platelets <25 x10^9/L
Liver function (serum ALT) - baseline, week 2, then monthly in chronic hepatitis C
Thyroid function (TSH) - baseline and every 3 months
Neuropsychiatric status - depression and suicidality at every visit
Eye examination - baseline for all patients; periodic if pre-existing retinopathy; promptly for new ocular symptoms
Triglycerides - periodically; consider discontinuation if persistently >=1000 mg/dL with pancreatitis symptoms
ECG/cardiac evaluation - baseline and during treatment in patients with cardiac disease or advanced cancer
Disease-specific response (hematologic counts, cytogenetics for CML; lesion measurements for Kaposi sarcoma)
counsel: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin; learn the proper technique and dispose of needles safely
A flu-like reaction (fever, chills, aches, tiredness) is common, especially early - taking it at bedtime and using acetaminophen can help
Tell your doctor right away if you feel depressed, hopeless, or have any thoughts of harming yourself
Do not switch between different brands of interferon without talking to your doctor - the dose may be different
Keep all appointments for blood tests, thyroid tests, and eye checks
Avoid alcohol, stay well hydrated, and use effective birth control during treatment
If on high doses, avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects your alertness
pk: Tumor/hematologic responses generally not seen for 1-3 months
Serum Tmax ~3.8 h after IM and ~7.3 h after SC dosing
Dosed daily or three times weekly depending on indication
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: BOXED WARNING: alpha-interferons cause or aggravate fatal/life-threatening neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders - monitor closely and withdraw if persistent or worsening
Flu-like syndrome (fever, fatigue, myalgia, headache, chills) is the most common toxicity and often improves over weeks
Do not switch interferon brands mid-regimen - dosage and adverse reactions differ between products
Contraindicated in hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh B/C) and autoimmune hepatitis; benzyl alcohol formulations are contraindicated in neonates/infants
Dosing is indication-specific and given in million IU (MIU); modify for toxicity by 50% reduction or interruption
Screen for and monitor depression/suicidality, thyroid dysfunction, retinopathy, and cardiac disease throughout therapy
missed: There is no specific missed-dose guidance in the FDA label. As a general practice, administer the missed dose when remembered unless it is near the time of the next scheduled dose, in which case skip it and resume the regular schedule; do not give a double dose. Confirm the plan with the prescriber, since dosing schedules differ by indication.
overdose: There are no reports of overdosage, but repeated large doses can cause profound lethargy, fatigue, prostration, and coma. There is no specific antidote. Management is hospitalization for close observation and supportive care, with monitoring and treatment of hematologic, hepatic, cardiac, and neuropsychiatric toxicities until recovery.
